knowledgePattern: Compare the averages of odd and even arithmetic subsequences

hints.title: Write each subsequence as an AP
hints.body: Identify the first term, last term and number of terms separately for the odd and even positions.
hints.recap: An AP sum is its number of terms multiplied by the average of its first and last terms.
hints.pitfall: Position parity does not tell you whether a term value itself is odd or even.

recall.reminder: An AP sum is its number of terms multiplied by the average of its first and last terms.

hints.title: Use the two given combinations
hints.body: Express both sums using the quantities you found, then use their difference and their total.
hints.recap: Symmetric AP terms have a common average, allowing a sum to be expressed compactly.
hints.pitfall: The two subsequences do not have the same number of terms.
hints.pause: Eliminate the shared average to determine n.

recall.reminder: Symmetric AP terms have a common average, allowing a sum to be expressed compactly.

solution:
1. Let the original first term be a, difference d, and middle term M=a+nd. The odd-position terms form an AP from a to a+2nd, so their average is M and their number is n+1.

2. The even-position AP runs from a+d to a+(2n−1)d, also with average M, and has n terms. Hence So=(n+1)M and Se=nM.

3. The difference gives M=5. The total gives (2n+1)5=505, so 2n+1=101 and n=50. Answer B.
